newsitem.title: USA: Visa says growth in US bankruptcies slowed in June.
newsitem.headline: Visa says growth in US bankruptcies slowed in June.

text.p: The number of Americans filing for personal bankruptcy rose 16.6 percent in June compared to the same period a year earlier, Visa USA said on Tuesday.
The rate of growth slowed from May, when bankruptcy filings rose 24.6 percent over May, 1996, Visa said citing data it collected from all filings in U.S. federal courts.
Based on the slowdown, Visa revised its forecast growth in personal bankruptcies for all of 1997 to 18.6 percent from 29.1 percent.

Filings rose 27.2 percent to 1.2 million in 1996 from 926,601 in 1995, according to the American Bankruptcy Institute. Filings hit a record 335,073 in the first quarter, the institute reported last month.

The bankruptcies have caused mounting losses for credit card issuers. Banks charged off $2.8 billion of bad credit card debt in the first quarter, up $560 million from a year earlier, bank regulators reported.
Visa and some of its member banks have called on Congress to change the bankruptcy code by making it more difficult for consumers to have credit card debts discharged.

Visa said in a statement that while it was "encouraged" by the decline in growth of new filings in June, it will "continue its work on reforming the bankruptcy code and promoting greater consumer education."
